rawItems.title: Huntingdonshire builder praised after iPhone alert detects crash near Chatteris
rawItems.content: A builder has been praised for his help at the scene of a crash after an iPhone alert notified police of the incident. The crash happened on Friday evening at the junction of Forty Foot Bank and Doddington Road near Chatteris. Two vehicles were involved and one overturned. Police said nobody was injured, although two people went to hospital as a precaution. Officers gave special thanks to Matt from Ramsey-based All Day Building. Not only did he help officers with the traffic and lend his jacket to one of those involved, but he also went the extra mile by helping to put the car back upright and move both vehicles to a safe location so the road was clear. The police spokesperson said: "All of your help is very much appreciated."

rawItems.title: Man arrested after woman sexually assaulted near Hunts junior school re-bailed
rawItems.content: Police have issued an update after a woman was sexually assaulted near a Huntingdonshire primary school. Officers were called at around 7.25am on May 26 with reports of a sexual assault on a woman in her 50s in Ramsey Road, St Ives. According to Cambridgeshire Constabulary, the incident is reported to have occurred near Westfield Junior School. A man in his 20s, from St Ives, was arrested this morning May 28 on suspicion of sexual assault and a public order offence. In an update this week, a spokesperson for the force confirmed the man has been re-bailed until September 26. Have you got a story you want to share? Get in touch at oliver.murphy@newsquest.co.uk

rawItems.title: Jail for uninsured driver who fled Cambs crash scene after killing pedestrian
rawItems.content: A uninsured driver from Cambridgeshire who fled the scene after hitting and killing a pedestrian has been jailed. Marcin Pilarski, 36, struck Sam Pope, 28, as he walked alongside Oil Mills Road, Ramsey Mereside, at just before 11pm on May 11, 2024. The crash was only reported when another driver called 999 after seeing Mr Pope, of Lincoln Road, Peterborough, laying in the road. Emergency services attended but despite their efforts, Mr Pope was declared dead at the scene. In a tribute, his family said: "Sam was a free spirit, who liked to live his life at 100mph and believed that rules were meant to be broken. "We shall miss his smile and crazy sense of humour that would always make you laugh, despite what mood you were in that day. "Sam was a rough diamond with a heart made of gold and will leave a big hole in our lives." Sam Pope was struck as he walked alongside Oil Mills Road (Image: Cambridgeshire Police) Less than an hour after the collision, at 11.40pm, police were called by Pilarski’s partner who told them he had returned home in her Vauxhall Astra. She revealed the car was badly damaged, with a smashed windscreen and headlamp, and that there was also blood on the front of the vehicle. The woman said that they lived 15 minutes, about nine and a half miles, from the scene of the fatal crash.
